description: This bar chart illustrates the distribution of samples across different reasoning categories within a dataset. The horizontal axis represents the reasoning categories, labeled “Mathematical Reasoning,” “General Reasoning,” “Natural Scene Reasoning,” “Physical Reasoning,” “Logical Puzzle Reasoning,” and “Chemical Reasoning,” listed in descending order based on sample count. The vertical axis, labeled “Number of Samples,” employs a logarithmic scale ranging from 10<sup>2</sup> to 10<sup>4</sup>, with tick labels at intervals of 10<sup>2</sup>.  Six gray bars are displayed, each corresponding to a reasoning category; the “Mathematical Reasoning” bar is the tallest, reaching approximately 7025 samples, while the “Chemical Reasoning” bar is the shortest, at approximately 49 samples. The “General Reasoning” bar reaches approximately 1709 samples, “Natural Scene Reasoning” reaches approximately 413 samples, “Physical Reasoning” reaches approximately 232 samples, and “Logical Puzzle Reasoning” reaches approximately 91 samples. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, outlining, or annotation.
